messages:
Sarah (Acme Corp): Hey folks — our rerank calls started failing this morning. ~10% of requests to /v1/rerank are returning 500. No obvious pattern except most failing requests contain emojis or copied text from Slack. sample payload attached.

Sarah (Acme Corp): curl example we used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"query": "Which of these is best? 🤔\nAlso includes a weird char: \u0000\", "candidates": ["Option A", "Opt\x00ion B", "Option C"]}'
```

Sarah (Acme Corp): Error body: `{\"error\":\"internal server error\"}` and response headers include `x-request-id` for several requests. Happening across EU and us-west. Can someone look? Our customers hit this in production. :grimacing:

Maya (Support): Thanks Sarah — escalating. Can you paste the x-request-id for a couple of failed calls? Also roughly what % of your traffic is rerank?

Sarah (Acme Corp): x-req: aa3f4c2, bb9d1aa. Rerank is ~30rps from our service, failures just started around 09:12 UTC.

Maya (Support): tagging eng — @Liam can you take a look?

Liam (Eng): on it. quick Qs: are these coming from a single client library version? and do you have any proxies that might mangle bytes?

Sarah (Acme Corp): single service, Node 18, using our internal HTTP wrapper. No charset overrides. We did copy/paste some content from Slack earlier (users pasting emojis).

Liam (Eng): reproducing locally with Sarah's payload now. getting a UnicodeDecodeError in the rerank worker logs when decoding candidates. stack snippet:
```py
File \"/srv/rerank/worker.py\", line 142, in process
  text = body.decode('utf-8')
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 23: invalid start byte
```

Liam (Eng): looks like there are invalid/overlong UTF-8 sequences (or embedded NULs). Our server assumed request bodies are valid UTF-8 and raised a 500 when decode fails.

Jun (Infra): tagging: we've seen similar before with some older proxies that mangle streams and leave lone continuation bytes. Also some clients base64-escape content incorrectly. Can you check if the Node wrapper double-encodes or passes raw buffers?

Sarah (Acme Corp): we don't do any base64. I'll grep our inputs for "\\x00" or high-bit bytes. Quick grep found "Opt\\x00ion" in one candidate — not visible in UI. Ugh. Looks like a sanitizer earlier in our pipeline replaced emoji with special byte sequence.

Maya (Support): summary so far: input can contain NUL (\u0000) or broken UTF-8 sequences, server throws on decode -> 500 to customer -> retries -> additional billable calls. Not ideal.

Liam (Eng): short-term mitigation: we can make the rerank endpoint reject non-UTF-8 with a 400 and clearer error, and log the offending bytes + request-id so customers can sanitize. Long term we should accept lossy decoding (errors='replace') for candidate text to avoid 500s.

Liam (Eng): proposed patch in PR:
```diff
- body = raw_body.decode('utf-8')
+ try:
+   body = raw_body.decode('utf-8')
+ except UnicodeDecodeError:
+   # fallback to replacement to avoid 500s; log and return 400 on strict mode
+   body = raw_body.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
+   logger.warn('utf8-decoding-fallback', request_id=req_id, sample=raw_body[:64])
```

Jun (Infra): also recommend normalizing NULs and control chars on the input path: replace NUL with U+FFFD or remove. Some downstream tokenizers choke on embedded \u0000.

Maya (Support): I've asked Sarah to apply a temporary client-side scrub so you can get immediate relief: replace /[\u0000-\u0008\u000B-\u000C\u000E-\u001F]/g with '' and ensure UTF-8 encode. Sarah, can you roll that today?

Sarah (Acme Corp): yes will do. rolling a quick patch to production now.

ops-bot: Deploy queued: tag=acme-scrub/2026-03-15T09:45

Sarah (Acme Corp): patch deployed, re-running failing requests — initial batches look good, 500s dropped to 0 for the endpoints we checked. :tada:

Liam (Eng): I'm opening the internal PR to make the server tolerant and to emit a clear error code when strict validation is enabled. We'll also add a metric for "decode-fallbacks" so SRE can alert.

Liam (Eng): tests added. plan is to canary for 30m on rerank workers in us-west then full rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy started: service=rerank-workers canary=us-west-1 version=2026.03.15-utf8-fallback

ops-bot: Deploy successful: canary healthy -> promoting

ops-bot: Deploy successful: global rollout complete version=2026.03.15-utf8-fallback

Maya (Support): quick note for billing: because some clients retried aggressively we saw duplicate billable requests for a subset. I've flagged finance to review refund for related x-request-ids.

Sarah (Acme Corp): confirmed all good on our side after the server rollout too. Thanks to the team for quick response.

Liam (Eng): follow-ups: 1) add better error payload when we reject non-UTF8, 2) doc update in API reference about allowed characters and suggestions for sanitizing, 3) work with devex to add common client-side sanitizer snippets (Node/Python).

Maya (Support): filing a KB article and pinging customer success to follow up with Sarah about refunds and impact.

Sarah (Acme Corp): appreciated! :clap:
